newsitem.title: UK: S&P says Nederlandse Waterschapsbank programme AAA.
newsitem.headline: S&P says Nederlandse Waterschapsbank programme AAA.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Monday it assigned AAA long-term and A1 plus short-term ratings to Nederlandse Waterschapsbank N.V.'s (NWB) existing five billion guilder multicurrency debt issuance programme.

"The bank's rating is based on its importance as an instrument of public policy in the Netherlands which is evidenced by strong support from the Ministry of Finance, the bank's excellent asset quality, low risk profile and sound profitability," S&P said in a statement.
According to NWB's Articles of Association, the bank can neither lend to nor be owned by the private sector, S&P said.
"The vast majority of lending is to state and local governments, water control boards, and housing associations, however, the bank also has a central treasury function for the water control boards.

"NWB operates independently, however, state support is evidenced by the bank's tax-exempt status and the representation of both the Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Transport and Public Works on the supervisory board. The bank's shareholders are all public sector entities," the agency said.

NWB, the Netherlands's sixth largest bank, has a loan portfolio comprised of Dutch public authorities and limited liability public utilities with the vast majority carrying a zero risk weighting under the Dutch regulators' interpretations of the BIS guidelines.
Although balance sheet leverage is very high, equity is only three percent of assets, NWB's loan portfolio is extremely low risk and the bank has never suffered a loan loss, S&P said.
"Despite the thin margins in public sector lending, NWB's small cost base allows for sustained profitability."
S&P said the outlook was stable. It expects NWB to remain devoted to its traditional Dutch public sector business.

"Although the market for public sector lending will continue to be increasingly competitive, NWB is well placed as a low cost, niche player whose public policy function remains undisputed and supported by the Dutch state," S&P said.
